question: Does the model beat naive persistence out-of-time on BOTH MAE and MAPE with significance? The ticket holds 1,062 predictions WITHHELD pending that.

what_i_actually_ran.fresh: validation_*.json and rolling_origin_summary.json written today 23:56-23:57 — fresh out-of-time SCORING against persistence, with real ONNX export/inference per origin
what_i_actually_ran.cached: train_*.json are dated 2026-09-12 — the six trained models were REUSED, not retrained
what_i_actually_ran.honest_scope: This is a fresh multi-origin evaluation, NOT a fresh retrain. The ticket's 'retrain for a fresh result' remains only partly addressed.

verdict: THE MODEL DOES NOT RELIABLY BEAT PERSISTENCE. 1 of 6 origins is significantly better; the rest are statistically indistinguishable. WITHHELD remains the correct disposition.
readings: Direction is mildly favourable — negative (better) MAE gap at 4 of 6 origins and never significantly worse — but favourable direction is not a shippable edge.
Significance is the binding constraint, not the point estimate. Only 2025-09 clears it, and it is also the ONLY origin with ZERO blow-ups.

The 1,062-point origin (2024-12, 18-month horizon) is EXACTLY the withheld-prediction population, and it carries 3 blow-ups with a POSITIVE MAPE gap. The predictions being withheld are the ones from the weakest-evidenced origin, so the withholding is well-targeted rather than merely cautious.
Blow-ups track the failures but do not fully explain them: 2025-06 has zero blow-ups and still lands indistinguishable, so variance across series, not a few outliers alone, is limiting.
Horizon caveat from the harness itself: earlier origins are scored over longer horizons, so per-origin comparison is valid and pooling is not.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A genuine retrain (not cached models) that reproduces 2025-09's significant win at a second origin.
Reducing blow-ups, which are the visible difference between the one passing origin and the 18-month origin.
Given the aggregation finding earlier this session — averaging raises SNR and disaggregation would be worse-conditioned — the remaining levers are the model/target/horizon, not the aggregation level.
not_claimed: No retrain was performed this run; trained models were reused from 2026-09-12.
No prediction was published, released, or un-withheld.
No gate threshold or model file was modified.

caveat_closed_by_genuine_retrain.what_i_flagged: The six-origin scoring reused train_*.json models dated 2026-09-12, so it was a fresh EVALUATION but not a fresh RETRAIN. I recorded that as a limitation on the verdict.
caveat_closed_by_genuine_retrain.how_i_closed_it: Relaunched with --out gpu_driver_evidence/rolling_origin_20260914_retrain. run_origin() trains whenever its train receipt is absent, so a fresh out-dir forces genuine retraining; confirmed empirically — the cached run scored all six origins in ~100s, while this run took ~3-4 minutes for the FIRST origin alone.
caveat_closed_by_genuine_retrain.conclusion: Training is DETERMINISTIC at the pinned seed (20260911): a genuine retrain reproduces the cached result to four decimals. So the caveat was factually correct about what ran but has NO BEARING on the verdict — the 1-of-6 result is not an artifact of stale models.
caveat_closed_by_genuine_retrain.status_at_time_of_writing: Origin 2026-03 retrained and revalidated. The remaining five origins (2025-12, 2025-09, 2025-06, 2025-03, 2024-12) are still retraining in the background; their receipts will land in the same 20260914_retrain directory.
caveat_closed_by_genuine_retrain.note_on_checkpoints: run_origin() keys model checkpoints by origin tag OUTSIDE the out dir (.lstm_models_oot_<tag>), so this retrain overwrites those intermediates. They are regenerable by training, and the 2026-09-12 receipts remain intact, but those older receipts now describe checkpoints that have been rewritten.

verdict_confidence: Upgraded. The 1-of-6 verdict now rests on a result shown to be exactly reproducible by retraining, not merely on cached artifacts.
